nfl.vote_outcome_model.mechanism: Winner or rank probability from candidate quality, narrative, previous votes, timing and electorate composition, aggregated through each award's actual ballot: the AP MVP is a 50-voter top-5 ranked ballot scored 10-5-3-2-1 (verified for 2023 and 2025; a 2022 start is supported by a headline only), and for the 2025 season all eight AP awards including Coach of the Year used a top-5 ballot scored 10-5-3-2-1; an earlier top-3 5-3-1 ballot for the non-MVP awards and single first-place voting before 2022 are UNVERIFIED and the place count must be read per season from the AP tally.
nfl.vote_outcome_model.measurement: Per AP award, model each voter's ranked ballot: rank-ordered (exploded) logit of candidate placements on features (team win% at ballot close, statistical rank within position by EPA or season totals, prior award wins, position dummy), ridge penalty by leave-one-season-out CV, prior weight 3 pseudo-observations; fit seasons whose full AP placement counts are published (five places for every AP award in 2025; earlier non-MVP place counts taken from each season's AP tally because the pre-2025 non-MVP ballot length is unverified) and any single-vote seasons on first-place votes only as a separate regime sharing feature weights through a hierarchical prior. Simulate 50 ballots per draw, score with 10-5-3-2-1 (MVP and, in 2025, every other AP award; use the scheme printed in that season's AP tally otherwise), winner = highest points (ties shared). Non-AP processes (PFWA Executive of the Year, Hall of Fame, All-Pro, T100) keep their own model: T100 ordered logit on previous rank, change in production, position group, age. Output P(candidate=winner) and P(rank=r); group markets P(group) = sum of P(win) by team at announcement time with 1/N co-winner payout; Executive of the Year tie probability = own-award co-winner frequency shrunk to comparable awards with weight 10. As-of ballot close.

nfl.teammate_vote_split_penalty.rationale: AP awards are ranked-points ballots (MVP 10-5-3-2-1 over five places; in the 2025 season the other AP awards were also top-5 10-5-3-2-1, earlier non-MVP schemes unverified), so two similar candidates split first places but not all support: a candidate can win on second- and third-place points (2025 MVP: Stafford 366 points with 24 firsts, Maye 361 with 23). A penalty fitted to first-place shares under plurality overstates the split for ranked seasons and must be estimated by regime.
nfl.teammate_vote_split_penalty.measurement: Rank-ordered logit latent utility for candidate i on voter ballot = x_i'theta - beta_r x max over same-team or same-position rivals j of x_j'theta, where x are the nfl.vote_outcome_model features and r indexes the placement (first place versus lower places). Estimate theta and beta_r by maximum likelihood on placement counts per candidate for seasons with published AP placement counts (five places per award in 2025; earlier place counts per the AP tally), and on first-place vote shares under a Dirichlet-multinomial for 2005-2021 single-vote seasons as a separate regime; ridge penalty by leave-one-season-out CV, shrink beta_r toward 0. Output winner probabilities from simulated 50-voter ballots scored by the award's point scheme. As-of ballot close.
